name: Frank Zappa
hook: A composer who mixed doo-wop, rock and modern classical music into satire, and whose son played guitar on Weird Al's Zappa pastiche.

blurb.age13: Frank Zappa was born in Baltimore in 1940. As a teenager he loved both doo-wop and the strange, noisy classical music of Edgard Varèse, and he spent his career mixing the two with rock and jokes. His band, the Mothers of Invention, released 'Freak Out!' in 1966, one of the first rock double albums. He said his band were satirists who made fun of everything. He also campaigned against censorship. He died in 1993.
blurb.adult: Born in Baltimore in 1940, Zappa formed the Mothers of Invention in 1965; 'Freak Out!' (Verve, 1966) was the second rock double album. His sources were R&B, doo-wop and modern composition, Varèse above all, and he described the Mothers' purpose as satire of everything. He disbanded them in 1969 for money reasons, recorded prolifically until his death in Los Angeles in 1993, and was a prominent anti-censorship campaigner. His son Dweezil, a guitarist, plays on Yankovic's 'Genius in France'.
